Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

anticipate verb

see coming and be ready

also anticipation, foresee, see it coming, in anticipation, look ahead

classical

Cic. Fam. 9.18.4: āctum dē tē est, nisi prōvidēs (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 5.8: reī frūmentāriae

prōvideō, prōvidēre, prōvīdī, prōvīsum

verb, second conjugation; with accusative, or dative (provide for), or nē

foresee; provide for, take care in advance

Both halves of “anticipate”: to see what is coming (quae ēventūra sunt prōvidēre) and to see to it in time (reī frūmentāriae prōvidēre, to make sure of supplies).

Other words

  • anticipō, anticipāre, anticipāvī, anticipātum — take beforehand, anticipate (a feeling, an event)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 8.14: quī anticipēs ejus reī molestiam, quam trīduō scītūrus sīs (Lewis & Short)

    To take something up before its time: to fret over news before it comes (Cicero, below), to die before one’s time (mortem, Suet. Tib. 61). Not “expect” (see wait).

  • praecipiō, praecipere, praecēpī, praeceptum — take in advance; enjoy in advance

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 13.45: praecipiō gaudia suppliciōrum vestrōrum (Antony, quoted; Lewis & Short)

    To get a pleasure or an advantage ahead of time; its everyday sense is to instruct, so the context must make this one plain.

Examples

  • āctum dē tē est, nisi prōvidēs

    you’re done for unless you look aheadCic. Fam. 9.18.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • quī anticipēs ejus reī molestiam, quam trīduō scītūrus sīs

    for you to suffer in advance over a matter you will know about in three daysCic. Att. 8.14 (Lewis & Short)

  • Hoc nēmō prōvīderat.

    Nobody had seen this coming.composed

See also predict, wait, look forward to, probably.
